perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'needed more ways for people and goods moved across it' — the governing pattern is 'ways for X to move across it': 'for people and goods' is the notional subject of a required to-infinitive complement of 'ways'. Alternative rescue parses were tested: (i) reduced relative 'people and goods [that were] moved across it' is formally constructible but logically circular (the city would be needing ways 'for goods already moved across', and 'ways for NP' is then left without its licensed infinitival complement, stranding the purpose semantics); (ii) no absolute/participial-adjunct reading yields a coherent clause. Must be 'to move' (or 'to be moved'). Ungrammatical — this is the answer.
